Students engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. Students will not receive credit for both MCWP 50 and MCWP 50R. Must be taken for a letter grade to satisfy the Muir College writing requirement.
courses.prerequisites_text: satisfaction of the MCWP 40 requirement or completion of IGETC.

courses.subject: MCWP
courses.title: Critical Writing
courses.description: Online version of the second course of sequence in reading and writing which satisfies the Muir College graduation requirement in writing. Required of all Muir College first-year students and of transfer students. MCWP 50R focuses on advanced skills of argument and analyses. Students engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. This class is held synchronously online. Students will not receive credit for both MCWP 50 and MCWP 50R. Must be taken for a letter grade to satisfy the Muir College writing requirement. This is a distance education course.

courses.subject: MCWP
courses.title: Argument and Analysis
courses.description: An advanced course in argumentation and analysis, with particular attention both to constructing arguments and analyzing the logic and rhetoric of others’ arguments. Students will engage in close reading of texts, weekly writing and revision, and individual conferences. MCWP 125 courses are for transfer students who enter Muir College with TAG or IGETC. Students may receive credit for one of the following: MCWP 125, MCWP 125R, MCWP 50, or MCWP 50R. Course must be taken for letter grade to fulfill Muir College writing requirement.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Fundamentals of Music B
courses.description: This course, second in a three-quarter sequence, focuses on understanding music theory and in developing musical ability through rhythm, ear training, and sight singing exercises. Topics include major and minor scales, seventh-chords, transposition, compound meter and rudiments of musical form.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 1A.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Basic Musicianship
courses.description: Primarily intended for music majors. Development of basic skills: perception and notation of pitch and temporal relationships. Introduction to functional harmony. Studies in melodic writing. Drills in sight singing, rhythmic reading, and dictation.
courses.prerequisites_text: passing score on proficiency exam or consent of instructor. Must be taken in sequence. Music majors must be concurrently enrolled in MUS 2AK, 2BK, and 2CK (Basic Keyboard).

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Basic Keyboard
courses.description: Scales, chords, harmonic progressions, transposition, and simple pieces.
courses.prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in MUS 2A, B, C.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Introduction to Western Music
courses.description: A brief survey of the history of Western music from the Middle Ages to the present. Much attention will be paid to the direct experience of listening to music and attendance of concerts. Class consists of lectures, listening labs, and live performances.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Electronic Music
courses.description: Lectures and listening sessions devoted to the most significant works of music realized through the use of computers and other electronic devices from the middle of this century through the present.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: American Music: Jazz Cultures
courses.description: Jazz is one of the primary foundations for American music in the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. This course highlights the multicultural and international scope of jazz by taking a thematic rather than a chronological approach to the subject, and by highlighting the music and lives of a diverse array of jazz practitioners from around the country and around the world. Students may not receive credit for both MUS 8 and MUS 8GS.
courses.prerequisites_text: none. (Offered in selected years.)

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Symphony
courses.description: This course will consist of lectures and listening sessions devoted to a detailed discussion of a selection of representative orchestral works (e.g., Mozart, Beethoven, Berlioz, Stravinsky, Ligeti, etc.).
courses.prerequisites_text: none. (Offered in selected years.)

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Opera
courses.description: A study of works from the history of opera to coincide when possible with operas presented in the San Diego opera season. Class consists of lectures, listening labs, live performances, and opera on video.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Worlds of Music
courses.description: Through surveying selected musical traditions and practices from around the world, this course explores the ways in which music both reflects and affects social, cultural, and ecological relationships. Specific case studies will be covered through lectures, films, and listening sessions.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Popular Music
courses.description: A course on popular music from different time periods, covered through lectures, films, and listening sessions. Topics vary from year to year. May be taken for credit twice.
courses.prerequisites_text: none.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Instrumental/Vocal Instruction
courses.description: Individual instruction on intermediate level in instrumental technique and repertory. For declared music majors and minors. Students must be simultaneously enrolled in a performance ensemble or nonperformance music course. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Vocal Instruction
courses.description: Individual instruction on intermediate level in vocal technique and repertory. For declared music majors and minors. Students must be simultaneously enrolled in a performance ensemble or nonperformance music course and in MUS 32VM. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Vocal Master Class
courses.description: All students enrolled in voice lessons (32V, 132V, or 132C) perform for one another and their instructors. Students critique in-class performances, with emphasis on presentation, diction, dramatic effect, vocal quality, and musicality.
courses.prerequisites_text: concurrent enrollment in MUS 32V, 132V, or 132C.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Department Seminar
courses.description: The department seminar serves both as a general department meeting and as a forum for the presentation of research and performances by visitors, faculty, and students. Required of all undergraduate music and music humanities majors every quarter a student is a declared music major. Four units or four quarters of enrollment are required of all undergraduate ICAM music majors who choose the MUS 43. Department Seminar option for their Visitor Series requirement. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit twelve times.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: First-year Student Seminar
courses.description: The First-year Student Seminar Program is designed to provide new students with the opportunity to explore an intellectual topic with a faculty member in a small seminar setting. First-year student seminars are offered in all campus departments and undergraduate colleges, and topics vary from quarter to quarter. Enrollment is limited to fifteen to twenty students, with preference given to entering first-year students.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Sustainable Well-Being/Music
courses.description: This experiential course teaches the art of practicing psychological well-being, based on Eastern and Western approaches (e.g., mindfulness, positive psychology, cognitive therapy, neuroscience, theatre and art), from the perspective of a musician. Each week there is a short lecture on a given topic, combined with workshop-style exercises.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music Theory and Practice II
courses.description: Study of tonal harmony and counterpoint. Analysis of Bach chorales and other music from the Baroque period. Musicianship studies: sight-singing, dictation, and keyboard skills.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 2C.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Seminar in Composition II
courses.description: Second part in composition course sequence. Intensive work in free composition by drafting a composition for presentation at the end of MUS 103C. Written analysis of contemporary repertoire is introduced. Instruction about calligraphic conventions including computer engraving programs.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 103A.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Honors Seminar in Composition
courses.description: Advanced individual projects for senior music majors pursuing honors in composition. Projects will be critically reviewed in seminar with fellow students and faculty composers.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 103A-B-C and admission into the Department of Music Honors Program in composition. Department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Critical Studies Seminar
courses.description: This seminar explores the history of music in relation to critical issues, such as race, gender, sexuality, the environment, and politics. Readings include recent literature in cultural studies, musicology, and sociology. Topics vary. May be taken for credit twice.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Restricted to music majors or consent of instructor; department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Topics/World Music Traditions
courses.description: A study of particular regional music in their repertory, cultural context, and interaction with other traditions. Topics vary. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Topics in Classic, Romantic, and Modern Music
courses.description: This course will focus on topics in Western music from 1750 to the early twentieth century. May be taken for credit five times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor. Department approval required. MUS 4, 8–10, or 120 recommended.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Music and Ideas Since 1900
courses.description: A critical examination of music from the early twentieth century to the present, focusing on the generation and embodiment of cultural ideas through and in music.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Women in Music
courses.description: A survey of the biographical, historical, sociological, and political issues affecting woman musicians, their creativity, their opportunities, and their perception by others. It compares and contrasts the work of women composers, performers, patrons, teachers, and writers on music from the Middle Ages through the present.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: History of Music in Western Culture II
courses.description: This sequence introduces key concepts, histories, and practices in contemporary music studies. In this course, students will develop original applications for research skills discussed in MUS 120A.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 120A. Music majors are recommended to take MUS 101B concurrently. Department approval required for nonmajors.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Discover Jazz
courses.description: Offers an introduction to jazz, including important performers and their associated styles and techniques. Explores the often-provocative role jazz has played in American and global society, the diverse perceptions and arguments that have surrounded its production and reception, and how these have been inflected by issues of race, class, gender, and sexuality. Specific topics vary from year to year. (Cross-listed with ETHN 179.)
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Chamber Music Performance
courses.description: Instruction in the preparation of small group performances of representative instrumental and vocal chamber music literature. May be taken for credit six times, after which students must enroll for zero units.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor through audition. Department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Advanced Improvisation Performance
courses.description: Master class instruction in advanced improvisation performance for declared majors and minors only or consent of instructor. Audition required at first class meeting. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor through audition. Department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Proseminar in Music Performance
courses.description: Individual or master class instruction in advanced instrumental performance. For declared music majors and minors. Students must be simultaneously enrolled in a performance ensemble or nonperformance music course. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Recital Preparation
courses.description: Advanced instrumental/vocal preparation for senior music majors pursuing honors in performance. Repertoire for a solo recital will be developed under the direction of the appropriate instrumental/vocal faculty member. Special audition required during Welcome Week preceding fall quarter.
courses.prerequisites_text: by audition only; MUS 132. Department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Proseminar in Vocal Instruction
courses.description: Individual instruction in advanced vocal performance. For declared music majors and minors. Students must be simultaneously enrolled in a performance ensemble or nonperformance music course and in the Vocal Master Class, MUS 32VM. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Symphonic Orchestra
courses.description: Repertoire is drawn from the classic symphonic literature of the eighteenth, nineteenth, and twentieth centuries with a strong emphasis on recently composed and new music. Distinguished soloists, as well as The La Jolla Symphony Chorus, frequently appear with the orchestra. The La Jolla Symphony Orchestra performs two full-length programs each quarter, each program being performed twice. May be taken for credit six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: audition and department approval required.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Jazz Theory and Improvisation
courses.description: Study of jazz theory and improvisation, focused on fundamental rhythmic, harmonic, melodic, and formal aspects of modern jazz style. Application of theoretical knowledge to instruments and concepts will be reinforced through listening, transcription work, and composition and improvisation exercises. Second course of a yearlong sequence; continuation of MUS 137A.
courses.prerequisites_text: MUS 137A or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Department Seminar
courses.description: The department seminar serves both as a general department meeting and as a forum for the presentation of research and performances by visitors, faculty, and students. Required of all undergraduate music majors every quarter.

courses.subject: MUS
courses.title: Senior Project in Computing Arts I
courses.description: Students pursue projects of their own design over two quarters with support from faculty in a seminar environment. Project proposals are developed, informed by project development guidelines from real world examples. Collaborations are possible. Two production-course limitation. Renumber from ICAM 160A. Students may receive credit for only one of the following: MUS 160A, VIS 160A, ICAM 160A.
courses.prerequisites_text: VIS 141B or VIS 145B or VIS 147B or MUS 172. Open to music and ICAM majors only. Department approval required.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Engineering Computation Using MATLAB
courses.description: Introduction to the solution of engineering problems using computational methods. Formulating problem statements, selecting algorithms, writing computer programs, and analyzing output using MATLAB. Computational problems from NanoEngineering, chemical engineering, and materials science are introduced. The course requires no prior programming skills. Cross-listed with CENG 15. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: NANO 15, NANO 15R, CENG 15, or CENG 15R.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Foundations in NanoEngineering: Physical Principles
courses.description: Introduction to quantum mechanics and nanoelectronics. Wave mechanics, the Schrödinger equation, free and confined electrons, band theory of solids. Nanosolids in 0D, 1D, and 2D. Application to nanoelectronic devices. Priority enrollment given to NanoEngineering majors.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20D and NANO 11. Priority given to NA25 majors.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Electronic Devices and Circuits for NanoEngineers
courses.description: Overview of electrical devices and CMOS integrated circuits emphasizing fabrication processes, and scaling behavior. Design, and simulation of submicron CMOS circuits including amplifiers active filters digital logic, and memory circuits. Limitations of current technologies and possible impact of nanoelectronic technologies.
courses.prerequisites_text: NANO 15, NANO 11, MATH 20B or MATH 20D, and PHYS 2B.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Molecular Modeling of Nanoscale Systems
courses.description: Principles and applications of molecular modeling and simulations toward NanoEngineering. Topics covered include molecular mechanics, energy minimization, statistical mechanics, molecular dynamics simulations, and Monte Carlo simulations. Students will get hands-on training in running simulations and analyzing simulation results. Prerequisites : MATH 20F or MATH 18, NANO 102, NANO 104, and NANO 15 or CENG 15 or MAE 8. Restricted to NanoEngineering majors or by department approval.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Probability and Statistical Methods for Engineers
courses.description: Probability theory, conditional probability, Bayes theorem, discrete random variables, continuous random variables, expectation and variance, central limit theorem, graphical and numerical presentation of data, least squares estimation and regression, confidence intervals, testing hypotheses. Cross-listed with CENG 114. Students may not receive credit for both NANO 114 and CENG 114.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20F or MATH 18 and NANO 15 or CENG 15 or MAE 8.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Multiscale Transport
courses.description: Introduction to basic transport phenomena relevant to nanoscale and general materials systems, including engineering units and pressure, heat conduction and convection, momentum transport and laminar flow, and diffusion in solids and fluids.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: NanoEngineering System Design I
courses.description: Principles of product design and the design process. Application and integration of technologies in the design and production of nanoscale components. Engineering economics. Initiation of team design projects to be completed in NANO 120B. Prerequisites : NANO 110.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Polymeric Materials
courses.description: Foundations of polymeric materials. Topics: structure of polymers; mechanisms of polymer synthesis; characterization methods using calorimetric, mechanical, rheological, and X-ray-based techniques; and electronic, mechanical, and thermodynamic properties. Special classes of polymers: engineering plastics, semiconducting polymers, photoresists, and polymers for medicine. Cross-listed with CENG 134 and CHEM 134. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: CENG 134, CHEM 134, NANO 134.
courses.prerequisites_text: CHEM 6C and PHYS 2C.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Mechanical Behavior of Materials
courses.description: Microscopic and macroscopic aspects of the mechanical behavior of engineering materials, with emphasis on recent development in materials characterization by mechanical methods. The fundamental aspects of plasticity in engineering materials, strengthening mechanisms, and mechanical failure modes of materials systems.
courses.prerequisites_text: NANO 108.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Research project as equivalent to a “senior thesis” can be approved for two NanoEngineering elective courses (eight units total). This course is taken as an elective on a P/NP basis. It must be done in consecutive quarters and the student must find a faculty member who will oversee the research project. Eligible students must have completed at least ninety units and must have a UC San Diego cumulative GPA of 3.0 or better. Detailed policy and procedures may be obtained from the Student Affairs Office.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Graduate Seminar in Chemical and Nano Engineering
courses.description: Each graduate student in chemical or nano engineering is expected to attend a weekly seminar dealing with current topics in nano and chemical engineering. Topics will vary. Cross-listed with CENG 205. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit up to four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Nanosystems Integration
courses.description: Scaling issues and hierarchical assembly of nanoscale components into higher order structures which retain desired properties at microscale and macroscale levels. Novel ways to combine top-down and bottom-up processes for integration of heterogeneous components into higher order structures. Cross-listed with CENG 215. Students may not receive credit for both NANO 205 and CENG 215.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Nanomanufacturing
courses.description: Fundamental nanomanufacturing science and engineering, top-down nanomanufacturing processes, bottom-up nanomanufacturing processes, integrated top-down and bottom-up nanofabrication processes, three-dimensional nanomanufacturing, nanomanufacturing systems, nanometrology, nanomanufactured devices for medicine, life sciences, energy, and defense applications.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Nanomachines and Nanorobots
courses.description: The structure and operational principles of different nature biomotors will be discussed. Related bio-inspired efforts aimed at developing artificial nanomotors will also be covered, along with the prospects of using biomotors and synthetic nanomotors in engineering environments.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: BioElectronics
courses.description: Topics include photolithographic techniques for high-density DNA microarray production, incorporation of CMOS control into electronic DNA microarrays, direct electronic detection technology, bio-fuel cells, highly integrated devices (lab-on-a-chip, in vivo biosensors, etc.) Form heterogeneous materials and components. Cross-listed with BENG 247B and ECE 247B.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and graduate standing.

courses.subject: NANO
courses.title: Graduate Research in NanoEngineering
courses.description: Graduate research in NanoEngineering. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit four times for a maximum of twelve units. Prerequisites : consent of instructor and graduate standing.

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Independent Research
courses.description: Laboratory research under the supervision of individual members of the faculty of the neurosciences department in one or a combination of neurosciences disciplines, e.g., neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, neurochemistry, neuropharmacology. (P/NP grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Neuroscience Research Rounds
courses.description: Neurosciences group faculty members and graduate students will present and discuss ongoing research. Attendance will be mandatory for first- and second-year graduate students. Faculty, advanced graduate students, medical students, postdoctoral trainees, and other interested parties are encouraged to attend. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Neurology General Clinical Selective Clerkship
courses.description: Provides opportunities for practical application of neurological skills to the understanding and treatment of a variety of clinical disorders of the nervous system.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of first two years of medical school. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Subintern Pediatric Neurology
courses.description: Subinterns are responsible for the primary care of hospitalized pediatric neurology patients under direct resident and attending physician supervision. Students will perform procedures such as lumbar puncture and participate in night call, daily teaching round, neurology grand rounds, and journal clubs.
courses.prerequisites_text: Neurology 401 or consent of instructor. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Neurology Outpatient
courses.description: The student will rotate through the general and subspecialty (stroke, epilepsy, headache, nerve, and muscle) neurology clinics based at UC San Diego Medical Center, Perlman, VAMC, and Children’s Hospital. There are lectures and clinical conferences.
courses.prerequisites_text: Neurosciences 401 or equivalent. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEU
courses.title: Clinical Independent Study
courses.description: Independent clinical study for medical students (S/U grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Neurosciences
courses.description: Specialized advanced topic areas in neurosciences will be addressed in an interactive seminar course format. A different specific topic will be considered each quarter as announced in advance. Students will each present an aspect of the topic area and participate in discussions.
courses.prerequisites_text: priority given to neuroscience PhD students, or consent of instructor. (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Neuroanatomy
courses.description: Neuroanatomy with functional correlates, concentrating on mammals but also including other chordates and other phyla. Includes laboratory sessions with whole brains, gross sections, and histology. Labs are often simultaneous with lectures to permit interactive identification and contextualization of anatomical structures.
courses.prerequisites_text: for neurosciences graduate students in major codes NE75 and NE78. Other disciplines may enroll with consent of instructor of record. (W)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Neurosciences Research Rotation
courses.description: Independent study. (S/U grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Neurosciences Research
courses.description: Independent study. (S/U grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: NEUG
courses.title: Apprenticeship Teaching
courses.description: Participation in the department teaching program is required of all students working toward a PhD. In general, students are not expected to teach in the first year but are required to serve as teaching assistants or tutors for one quarter at any time during their subsequent years of training. The amount of teaching required is equivalent to the duties expected of a 50 percent assistant for one quarter.
courses.prerequisites_text: neurosciences graduate students. (S/U grades only.) (F,W,S)

courses.subject: SPPS
courses.title: Acute Care Adv Pharm Pract Exp

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
courses.description: A general introduction to some of the fundamental questions, texts, and methods of philosophy. Multiple topics will be covered, and may include the existence of God, the nature of mind and body, free will, ethics and political philosophy, knowledge and skepticism. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Logic
courses.description: Basic concepts and techniques in both informal and formal logic and reasoning, including a discussion of argument, inference, proof, and common fallacies, and an introduction to the syntax, semantics, and proof method in sentential (propositional) logic. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy: Ethics
courses.description: An inquiry into the nature of morality and its role in personal or social life by way of classical and/or contemporary works in ethics. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Science and Pseudoscience
courses.description: The differences among good science, bad science, and pseudoscience. Topics include the philosophical and practical demarcation problems; science and values; probabilistic fallacies, cognitive biases, and perceptual illusions; causation versus correlation, the placebo effect; why and when science is trustworthy; and case studies ranging from ESP to homeopathy to climate change denialism. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Ethics and Society
courses.description: An examination of ethical principles (e.g., utilitarianism, individual rights, etc.) and their social and political applications to contemporary issues: abortion, environmental protection, and affirmative action. Ethical principles will also be applied to moral dilemmas in government, law, business, and the professions. Warren College students must take course for a letter grade in order to satisfy the Warren College general-education requirement. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: CAT 2 and 3 or CAT 2CE and 3CE or CCE 1 and 2 or DOC 2 and 3 or HUM 1 and 2 or MCWP 40 and 50 or MCWP 40R and 50R or MMW 12 and 13 or WCWP 10A and B or SYN 1 and 2 or WARR 11A and 11B or SYN 1R and 2R.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Ethics and Society II
courses.description: An examination of a single set of major contemporary social, political, or economic issues (e.g., environmental ethics, international ethics) in light of ethical and moral principles and values. Warren College students must take course for a letter grade in order to satisfy the Warren College general-education requirement. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHIL 27 or POLI 27.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Ancient Philosophy
courses.description: A survey of classical Greek philosophy with an emphasis on Socrates, Plato and Aristotle, though some consideration may be given to Pre-Socratic and/or Hellenistic philosophers. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy between Reason and Despair
courses.description: Introduction to nineteenth-century philosophy, focusing on skepticism about the authority of reason to answer questions about the ultimate meaning and value of human life. Figures discussed may include Kant, Schopenhauer, Kierkegaard, Nietzsche, Goldman, and de Beauvoir. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Love and Sex
courses.description: This course will focus on philosophical topics surrounding love and sex by examining both historical and contemporary texts. We will discuss love and sex from a number of different angles and perspectives, and focus on issues such as the nature of love both as a mental and social phenomenon; different kinds of love and their demands on us; the connection between love and sex; the ethics and politics of love, sex, and marriage; and sex and consent. May not be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Plato
courses.description: A study of Socrates and/or Plato through major dialogues of Plato. Possible topics include the virtues and happiness; weakness of the will; political authority and democracy; the theory of Forms and sensible flux; immortality; relativism, skepticism, and knowledge. May be repeated for credit with change of content and approval of instructor. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: History of Philosophy: Early Modern
courses.description: An examination of seventeenth- and eighteenth-century philosophy, focusing on major works of Descartes, Locke, and Hume. PHIL 110, PHIL 111, and PHIL 112 should be taken in order. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHIL 110, upper-division standing and department stamp or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Logic
courses.description: Topics vary from year to year. They include Metalogic (Mathematical Logic), Modal Logic, Foundations of Logic, Foundations of Set Theory, Gödel’s Incompleteness Theorems, and others. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHIL 120 or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Epistemology
courses.description: Central problems in epistemology such as skepticism; a priori knowledge; knowledge of other minds; self-knowledge; the problem of induction; foundationalist, coherence, and causal theories of knowledge. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Moral Psychology
courses.description: The nature of action and psychological explanation. Topics include action individuation, reasons as causes, psychological laws, freedom and responsibility, weakness of will, self-deception, and the emotions. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Social Science
courses.description: Philosophical issues of method and substance in the social sciences, such as causal and interpretive models of explanation, structuralism and methodological individualism, value neutrality, and relativism. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Latinx Philosophy
courses.description: Philosophical issues surrounding Latina/o/x peoples, which may include debates about the nature, function, and stability of this identity; social and political issues, such as immigration, economics, racial politics, and justice; phenomenological and existential accounts of latinidad; Latina feminism; and the relationship of these concerns to other philosophical traditions. May not be repeated for credit.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Ethical Theory
courses.description: Systematic and/or historical perspectives on central issues in ethical theory such as deontic, contractualist, and consequentialist conceptions of morality; rights and special obligations; the role of happiness and virtue in morality; moral conflict; ethical objectivity and relativism; and the rational authority of morality. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics in the History of Ethics
courses.description: Central issues and texts in the history of ethics. Subject matter can vary, ranging from one philosopher (e.g., Confucius, Aristotle, Kant, or Mill) to a historical tradition (e.g., Greek ethics or the British moralists). May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Contemporary Moral Issues
courses.description: An examination of contemporary moral issues, such as abortion, euthanasia, war, affirmative action, and freedom of speech. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Biomedical Ethics
courses.description: Moral issues in medicine and the biological sciences, such as patient’s rights and physician’s responsibilities, abortion and euthanasia, the distribution of health care, experimentation, and genetic intervention. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Law
courses.description: A study of issues in analytical jurisprudence such as the nature of law, the relation between law and morality, and the nature of legal interpretation and issues in normative jurisprudence such as the justification of punishment, paternalism and privacy, freedom of expression, and affirmative action. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy and Race
courses.description: A philosophical investigation of the topics of race and racism. The role of “race” in ordinary speech. The ethics of racial discourse. Anthropological and biological conceptions of race. The social and political significance of racial categories. Post-racialist conceptions of race. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy and Literature
courses.description: A study of philosophical themes contained in selected fiction, drama, or poetry, and the philosophical issues that arise in the interpretation, appreciation, and criticism of literature. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Religion
courses.description: A general introduction to the philosophy of religion through the study of classical and/or contemporary texts. Among the issues to be discussed are the existence and nature of God, the problem of evil, the existence of miracles, the relation between reason and revelation, and the nature of religious language. May be repeated for credit two times with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing or consent of instructor. May be taken for credit twice with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy Honors
courses.description: Independent study by special arrangement with and under the supervision of a faculty member, including a proposal for the honors essay. An IP grade will be awarded at the end of this quarter; a final grade will be given for both quarters at the end of 191B.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval; consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: The Honors Essay
courses.description: Continuation of 191A: independent study by special arrangement with and under the supervision of a faculty member, leading to the completion of the honors essay. A letter grade for both 191A and 191B will be given at the end of this quarter.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Pedagogy and Learning Apprenticeship
courses.description: Under the supervision of an instructor, undergraduate students gain teaching experience through practical experiences in course management and effective teaching methods. Pedagogy and learning apprentices must have a minimum overall grade point average of 3.0. A student may not apprentice more than once for the same course for credit or for more than one course in the same quarter. May be repeated for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Directed Individual Study
courses.description: Directed individual study by special arrangement with and under the supervision of a faculty member. (P/NP grades only.) May be repeated for credit four times with change of content and approval of instructor.
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Colloquium in Science Studies
courses.description: A forum for the presentation and discussion of research in progress in science studies by graduate students, faculty, and visitors. Students must attend the colloquium series for their entire first and second years. May be taken for credit two times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Science Studies Part II
courses.description: Continuing the introduction developed in Part I, this course examines recent key topics and problem situations in science studies. Emphasis is on recent theoretical perspectives and empirical studies in communication, history, philosophy, and sociology of science and technology, and the interplay between them. Students may receive credit for one of the following: ANTH 269, COGR 225D, HIGR 241, PHIL 209D, or SOCG 255D.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Eighteenth-Century Philosophy
courses.description: A study of selected texts or topics from philosophers of the eighteenth century: for example, Kant or Hume. May be taken for credit six times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Science
courses.description: This seminar will cover current books and theoretical issues in the philosophy of science. May be taken for credit seven times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Latin American Philosophy
courses.description: Contemporary or historical approaches to philosophy in or concerned with Latin America. May focus on particular countries (e.g., Mexico, Peru), specific time periods (e.g., the nineteenth century), particular topics or movements (e.g., political liberalism, the philosophy of liberation), or specific figures (e.g., Alberdi, vaz Ferreira, Castellanos). May be taken for credit six times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Political Philosophy
courses.description: Topics may include the nature and limits of state authority, liberty and equality, distributive justice, liberalism and its critics (e.g., feminists, libertarians, and others), or issues in jurisprudence. The focus may be on classic texts or contemporary authors. May be taken for credit six times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Agency, Morality, and Psychology Research Group
courses.description: This course is designed for students to gain feedback from students and faculty on works in progress on the topics of agency, morality, and psychology, and on contemporary research on these topics. The course is suitable for those specializing in moral psychology, agency, ethics, and philosophy mind and psychology, and for those with special interests in the topics.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: German Philosophy Reading Group
courses.description: This course meets regularly to discuss primary or secondary literature in the area of German philosophy (including Kant, Fichte, Hegel, etc.). The reading is designed both for students doing active research in the field and for those seeking to gain some familiarity with it. Nongraduate students may enroll with consent of instructor. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit twenty-one times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Phenomenology Reading Group
courses.description: This course meets biweekly with students reading and presenting material from the phenomenological literature. The course is designed both for students doing active research in phenomenology and for those seeking to gain some familiarity with that tradition. Can be taken nine times for credit with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics and Methods in Contemporary Philosophy
courses.description: Investigation of central issues in contemporary philosophy. Content varies but typically will center on a recent and important philosophical book. Can be taken nine times for credit with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: History of Philosophy Research and Methods
courses.description: This course meets to discuss work in progress in the history of philosophy. Its aim is to introduce understanding of the methods and standards of research in the field through constructive criticism of each other’s work. Can be taken nine times for credit with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics and Methods in Ethics
courses.description: Weekly or biweekly meetings to discuss recent literature in ethics, broadly construed so as to include ethical theory, normative ethics, jurisprudence, and historical traditions in these fields. The course is suitable for those specializing in ethics and for those seeking some familiarity with the field. Can be taken nine times for credit with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Topics and Methods in Latin American Philosophy
courses.description: This course is designed for students to gain feedback from students and faculty on works in progress on Latin American philosophy. The course is suitable for those specializing in historical and contemporary philosophy in Latin America and for those with special interests in the topics.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Philosophy of Physics Reading Group
courses.description: A research group for graduate students engaged in philosophy or history of the physical sciences. The group discusses physical, historical, and philosophical articles and books and ongoing research projects. Can be taken nine times for credit with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Greek Reading Group
courses.description: This group provides training in reading and translating philosophical Greek by having students prepare translations of passages and lead discussions. The group helps train graduate students preparing for Departmental Greek Exam. Can be taken nine times for credit with change of content.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Directed Independent Study
courses.description: Supervised study of individually selected philosophical topics. S/U grades permitted.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Research Topics
courses.description: Advanced individual research studies under the direction of a member of the staff. Hours of outside preparation will vary with number of units taken. May be taken for credit nine times with changed content.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: S/U grades permitted.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: A course designed to satisfy the requirement that graduate students should serve as teaching assistants, either in the Department of Philosophy or in one of the writing programs offered by the various colleges. Each PhD candidate must teach the equivalent of quarter time for three academic quarters. Students are permitted to sign up as TAs for a maximum of eighteen quarters.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Professional Practice III
courses.description: The third in a series of four lecture-based courses dedicated to defining professionalism for healthcare providers. Lectures, readings, and discussion topics focus on building effective interdisciplinary healthcare teams and the science of quality improvement.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75).

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Medicine II
courses.description: The second in a series of four lecture-based courses studying the clinical presentation, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of patients seeking care for common medical conditions in primary and specialty care settings.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 214 and PAE 223.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Pharmacology and Pharmacotherapeutics II
courses.description: The second in a series of four lecture-based courses that explores the knowledge and concepts required to safely prescribe and monitor medications used to diagnose and treat common medical conditions in primary care and emergency department settings.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 214 and PAE 223.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Perioperative Medicine
courses.description: This lab-based course introduces learners to the roles and responsibilities of the perioperative healthcare team, and the unique needs of patients preparing for, undergoing, and recuperating from surgery. Demonstrating the knowledge and ability to perform perioperative technical skills is required.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75).

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Reasoning II
courses.description: The second in a series of four lecture- and lab-based courses designed to engage learners in team-based activities that require them to integrate newly acquired knowledge and skill to develop and strengthen their clinical reasoning ability.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 212, PAE 215, and PAE 216.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Diagnostic Studies II
courses.description: The second of a two-part series designed to provide learners with an overview of common diagnostic tests utilized during patient evaluation, diagnosis, and monitoring. Clinical indications for and accurate interpretation of electrocardiography, x-rays, computed tomography, MRI, and ultrasound are included.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75).

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: The Pediatric Patient
courses.description: This course will equip learners with the knowledge and skills required to evaluate and manage infants, children, adolescents, and their families in primary care settings. Topics include age-related considerations during the history and physical exam and recognizing/reporting abuse or neglect.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75).

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics courses are reserved for learners who require extra time to complete the clinical phase of training due to factors such as hardship, leave of absence, remediation, or deceleration. Credit hours vary.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and departmental approval required.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Family Medicine Rotation
courses.description: This supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the clinical evaluation and management of patients seeking preventive, urgent, acute, and chronic care in a primary care setting. Encounters will include experience with infants, children, adolescents, adults, and elderly.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Internal Medicine Rotation
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the comprehensive, longitudinal care of adult patients in an internal medicine specialty.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Pediatric Rotation
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the care of patients in the primary care specialty of pediatrics which focuses on the care of patients from birth to adolescence through young adulthood.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Women’s Health Rotation
courses.description: This supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the clinical evaluation and management of patients seeking women’s health, to include prenatal and gynecologic care. Encounters will include adolescents, adults, and elderly.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Mental and Behavioral Health Rotation
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the care of patients seeking behavioral and mental healthcare across the lifespan. Learners will participate in the evaluation and management of patients with mental and behavioral health concerns.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Surgery Rotation
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the care of patients in a surgical specialty. Emphasis will include a focus on the physician assistant’s role as a member of the surgical management team.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Emergency Medicine Rotation
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in the care of patients in an emergency department setting with a focus on the evaluation and management of patients who present with acute, traumatic, urgent, and emergent medical needs.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Elective Rotation I
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in a medical or surgical discipline. Learners will elect additional experiences in a specialty of their choice in settings that include inpatient, outpatient, surgery, urgent care, and the emergency department.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Elective Rotation II
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in a medical or surgical discipline. Learners will elect additional experiences in a specialty of their choice in settings that include inpatient, outpatient, surgery, urgent care, and the emergency department.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Elective Rotation III
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience requires active participation in a medical or surgical discipline. Learners will elect additional experiences in a specialty of their choice in settings that include inpatient, outpatient, surgery, urgent care, and the emergency department.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Independent Study Rotation
courses.description: This four-week non-clinical experience provides the learner with time to focus their efforts on completing their capstone project. Learners will also create a self-directed learning plan to prepare for final written and practical summative assessments required for graduation.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 410, PAE 411, PAE 412, PAE 420, PAE 430, PAE 440, and PAE 450.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Primary Care Selective Rotation I
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience is designed for learners with a commitment to a career in primary care. This experience places emphasis on continuity of care and the unique aspects of providing healthcare in a community and ambulatory setting.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Primary Care Selective Rotation II
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience is designed for learners with a commitment to a career in primary care. This experience places emphasis on continuity of care and the unique aspects of providing healthcare in a community and ambulatory setting.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Primary Care Selective Rotation III
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical practice experience is designed for learners with a commitment to a career in primary care. This experience places emphasis on continuity of care and the unique aspects of providing healthcare in a community and ambulatory setting.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Specialty Care Selective Rotation I
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical experience requires active participation in a specialty/sub-specialty setting. Learners choose clinical experiences with a common thread across three courses. This experience will enhance the learner’s understanding of the role of a physician assistant within the selected discipline.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Specialty Care Selective Rotation II
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical experience requires active participation in a specialty/sub-specialty setting. Learners choose clinical experiences with a common thread across three courses. This experience will enhance the learner’s understanding of the role of a physician assistant within the selected discipline.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Specialty Care Selective Rotation III
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical experience requires active participation in a specialty/sub-specialty setting. Learners choose clinical experiences with a common thread across three courses. This experience will enhance the learner’s understanding of the role of a physician assistant within the selected discipline.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Rural and Border Health Selective Rotation I
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical experience requires participation in a rural or border health setting. Learners choose clinical experiences with a common thread across three courses to enhance their understanding of the role of a physician assistant within the selected discipline.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Rural and Border Health Selective Rotation II
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical experience requires participation in a rural or border health setting. Learners choose clinical experiences with a common thread across three courses to enhance their understanding of the role of a physician assistant within the selected discipline.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Rural and Border Health Selective Rotation III
courses.description: This four-week supervised clinical experience requires participation in a rural or border health setting. Learners choose clinical experiences with a common thread across three courses to enhance their understanding of the role of a physician assistant within the selected discipline.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Independent Study for Clinical Concentrations
courses.description: This four-week non-clinical experience provides learners on a clinical concentration path with time to focus on completing their capstone project. Learners will also create a self-directed learning plan to prepare for final written and practical summative assessments required for graduation.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 410, PAE 411, PAE 412, PAE 420, PAE 430, PAE 440, and PAE 450.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Capstone
courses.description: The first of four one-week seminars designed to augment supervised clinical practice experiences wherein learners will apply the knowledge, skills, and attitudes acquired throughout the MAS-PAS program of study. A letter grade for each seminar will be assigned upon completion of seminar IV (PAE 494).
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Capstone II
courses.description: The second of four one-week seminars designed to augment supervised clinical practice experiences wherein learners will apply the knowledge, skills, and attitudes acquired throughout the MAS-PAS program of study. A letter grade for each seminar will be assigned upon completion of seminar IV (PAE 494).
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Capstone III
courses.description: The third of four one-week seminars designed to augment supervised clinical practice experiences wherein learners will apply the knowledge, skills, and attitudes acquired throughout the MAS-PAS program of study. A letter grade for each seminar will be assigned upon completion of seminar IV (PAE 494).
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Clinical Capstone IV
courses.description: The fourth of four one-week seminars designed to augment supervised clinical practice experiences wherein learners will apply the knowledge, skills, and attitudes acquired throughout the MAS-PAS program of study. A letter grade for each seminar will be assigned upon completion of seminar IV (PAE 494).
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Program to Practice
courses.description: This seminar course examines topics to the transition from the role the physician assistant learner to professional practice, including career development, contract negotiation, financial literacy, debt management, medical liability, risk management, licensing and credentialing process, and post-graduate education opportunities.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290 and PAE 494.

courses.subject: PAE
courses.title: Comprehensive Review
courses.description: This seminar course offers the physician assistant learner a seminar designed to synthesize didactic and clinical education and training as it applies to preparation for the Physician Assistant National Certification Examination (PANCE). Test-taking skills and high-yield preparation strategies are discussed.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Physician Assistant Education Program (PE75) and successful completion of PAE 290 and PAE 494.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mechanics
courses.description: First quarter of a three-quarter introductory physics course, geared toward life-science majors. Equilibrium and motion of particles in one and two dimensions in the framework of Newtonian mechanics, force laws (including gravity), energy, momentum, rotational motion, conservation laws, and fluids. Examples will be drawn from astronomy, biology, sports, and current events. PHYS 1A and 1AL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both. Students continuing to PHYS 1B/1BL will also need MATH 10B or 20B.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A or 20A. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mechanics Laboratory
courses.description: Physics laboratory course to accompany PHYS 1A. Experiments in Mechanics. PHYS 1A and 1AL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both. Students continuing to PHYS 1B/1BL will also need MATH 10B or 20B.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A or 20A. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in PHYS 1A and MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Second quarter of a three-quarter introductory physics course geared toward life-science majors. Electric fields, magnetic fields, DC and AC circuitry. PHYS 1B and 1BL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1A or 2A, and MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism Laboratory
courses.description: Physics laboratory course to accompany PHYS 1B. Experiments in electricity and magnetism. Program or materials fee may apply. PHYS 1B and 1BL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1A or 2A, 1AL or 2BL, and MATH 10B or 20B. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in PHYS 1B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Waves, Optics, and Modern Physics
courses.description: Third quarter of a three-quarter introductory physics course geared toward life-science majors. The physics of oscillations and waves, vibrating strings and sound, and the interaction of light with matter as illustrated through optics and quantum mechanics. Examples from biology, sports, medicine, and current events. PHYS 1C and 1CL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1B or 2B, and MATH 10B or 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Waves, Optics, and Modern Physics Laboratory
courses.description: Physics laboratory course to accompany PHYS 1C. Experiments in waves, optics, and modern physics. Program or materials fee may apply. PHYS 1C and 1CL are designed to be taken concurrently but may be taken in separate terms; taking the lecture before the lab is the best alternative to enrolling in both.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 1B or 2B, 1BL or 2CL, and MATH 10B or 20B. Recommended preparation: concurrent or prior enrollment in PHYS 1C.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Mechanics
courses.description: A calculus-based science-engineering general physics course covering vectors, motion in one and two dimensions, Newton’s first and second laws, work and energy, conservation of energy, linear momentum, collisions, rotational kinematics, rotational dynamics, equilibrium of rigid bodies, oscillations, gravitation. Students continuing to PHYS 2B/4B will also need MATH 20B. Students will not receive credit for both PHYS 2A and PHYS 2AR.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 10A-B or 20A or 20B or 20C or 31BH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Continuation of PHYS 2A covering charge and matter, the electric field, Gauss’s law, electric potential, capacitors and dielectrics, current and resistance, electromotive force and circuits, the magnetic field, Ampere’s law, Faraday’s law, inductance, electromagnetic oscillations, alternating currents and Maxwell’s equations. Students continuing to PHYS 2C will also need MATH 20C or 31BH.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A and MATH 20B or 20C or 31BH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20C or 31BH.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Fluids, Waves, Thermodynamics, and Optics
courses.description: Continuation of PHYS 2B covering fluid mechanics, waves in elastic media, sound waves, temperature, heat and the first law of thermodynamics, kinetic theory of gases, entropy and the second law of thermodynamics, Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves, geometric optics, interference and diffraction. Students continuing to PHYS 2D will need MATH 20D.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A, and MATH 20C or 31BH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20D. Prior completion of PHYS 2B is strongly recommended.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Laboratory—Electricity and Magnetism
courses.description: Experiments on L-R-C circuits; oscillations, resonance and damping, measurement of magnetic fields. One hour lecture and three hours laboratory. Program or materials fee may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A, and 2B or 4C. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in PHYS 2C or 4D.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics—Relativity and Quantum Physics
courses.description: A modern physics course covering atomic view of matter, electricity and radiation, atomic models of Rutherford and Bohr, relativity, X-rays, wave and particle duality, matter waves, Schrödinger’s equation, atomic view of solids, natural radioactivity.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A or 4A, 2B, and MATH 20D. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20E.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics for Physics Majors–Mechanics
courses.description: The first quarter of a five-quarter calculus-based physics sequence for physics majors and students with a serious interest in physics. The topics covered are vectors, particle kinematics and dynamics, work and energy, conservation of energy, conservation of momentum, collisions, rotational kinematics and dynamics, equilibrium of rigid bodies, small oscillations, gravitation, and central force motion.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20A. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20B and a knowledge of vectors.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics for Physics Majors—Electromagnetic Waves, Special Relativity and Optics
courses.description: Continuation of PHYS 4C covering electric and magnetic fields in matter, Maxwell’s equations and electromagnetic waves, special relativity and its applications to electromagnetism, optics, interference, diffraction.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 4A-B-C or the combination of PHYS 4C and PHYS 2A-B-C, MATH 20A-B-C or 31BH, 20E or 31CH, and 18 or 20F or 31AH. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in MATH 20D.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Energy and the Environment
courses.description: A course covering energy fundamentals, energy use in an industrial society and the impact of large-scale energy consumption. It addresses topics on fossil fuel, heat engines, solar energy, nuclear energy, energy conservation, transportation, air pollution and global effects. Concepts and quantitative analysis.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Introductory Special Topics
courses.description: From time to time a member of the regular faculty or a resident visitor will give a self-contained course on an introductory topic in their special area of research or help students prepare to succeed in the physics major. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only. May be repeated up to six times, provided the same topic is not repeated.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Introductory Special Topics Lab
courses.description: From time to time a member of the regular faculty or a resident visitor will offer a freshman-sophomore-level experimental lab in their special area of research. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only. May be repeated up to six times, provided the same topic is not repeated.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Scientific Computing with Python
courses.description: This course is designed for students concurrently enrolled in the PHYS 4 series and is an introduction to computer programming and scientific computing with Python. The course covers basic data structures and operations in Python and how to write and debug functions. These tools are then applied to scientific computing, including data analysis and visualization, numerical computations, and simulations. Recommended preparation: prior or concurrent enrollment in PHYS 4A.
courses.prerequisites_text: MATH 20A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Electromagnetism II
courses.description: Magnetic fields and magnetostatics, magnetic materials, induction, AC circuits, displacement currents; development of Maxwell’s equations.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 100A, MATH 20A, 20B, 20C or 31BH, 20D, 20E or 31CH, and 18 or 20F or 31AH. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mathematical and Computational Physics I
courses.description: A combined analytic and mathematically based numerical approach to the solution of common applied mathematics problems in physics and engineering. Topics: Fourier series and integrals, special functions, initial and boundary value problems, Green’s functions; heat, Laplace and wave equations.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 4B-C-D-E, MATH 20A-B-C or 31BH, 20D, 20E or 31CH, and 18 or 20F or 31AH. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Mechanics II
courses.description: Noninertial reference systems, dynamics of rigid bodies, Hamilton’s equations, Liouville’s theorem, chaos, continuum mechanics, special relativity.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 110A, MATH 20A-B-C or 31BH, 20D, 20E or 31CH, and 18 or 20F or 31AH. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Laboratory Projects
courses.description: A laboratory-lecture-project course featuring creation of an experimental apparatus in teams of about two. Emphasis is on electronic sensing of the physical environment and actuating physical responses. The course will use a computer interface such as the Arduino. PHYS 124 was formerly numbered PHYS 120B. Program or materials fees may apply.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 120.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Physics I
courses.description: Development of quantum mechanics. Wave mechanics; measurement postulate and measurement problem. Piece-wise constant potentials, simple harmonic oscillator, central field and the hydrogen atom. Three hours lecture, one-hour discussion session.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 4A-B-C-D-E, 100A, 110A. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Physics III
courses.description: Quantized electromagnetic fields and introductory quantum optics. Symmetry and conservation laws. Introductory many-body physics. Density matrix, quantum coherence and dissipation. The relativistic electron. Three-hour lecture, one-hour discussion session.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 130B.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Special Topics
courses.description: From time to time a member of the regular faculty or a resident visitor will give a self-contained short course on a topic in his or her special area of research. This course is not offered on a regular basis, but it is estimated that it will be given once each academic year. Course may be taken for credit up to two times as topics vary (the course subtitle will be different for each distinct topic). Students who repeat the same topic in PHYS 139 will have the duplicate credit removed from their academic record.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 2A-B-C-D or 4A-B-C-D-E, MATH 20A-B-C or 31BH, and 18 or 20F or 31AH.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Statistical and Thermal Physics II
courses.description: Applications of the theory of ideal quantum gases in condensed matter physics, nuclear physics and astrophysics; advanced thermodynamics, the third law, chemical equilibrium, low temperature physics; kinetic theory and transport in nonequilibrium systems; introduction to critical phenomena including mean field theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 130B and 140A. Open to major codes PY26, PY28, PY29, PY32, PY33, PY34, and PY35 only.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics
courses.description: Physics of the solid-state. Binding mechanisms, crystal structures and symmetries, diffraction, reciprocal space, phonons, free and nearly free electron models, energy bands, solid-state thermodynamics, kinetic theory and transport, semiconductors.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 130A or CHEM 130. Corequisites: PHYS 140A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Stars and Compact Objects
courses.description: A first course on stars, their structure, evolution, and as testing grounds for physics in extreme environments. Topics include fundamental interactions and nuclear physics in stars, fluid dynamics and transport equations, white dwarfs and neutron stars, supernovae, and the formation of heavy elements.
courses.prerequisites_text: 4A-B-C-D-E.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Biophysics of Neurons and Networks
courses.description: Information processing by nervous system through physical reasoning and mathematical analysis. A review of the biophysics of neurons and synapses and fundamental limits to signaling by nervous systems is followed by essential aspects of the dynamics of phase coupled neuronal oscillators, the dynamics and computational capabilities of recurrent neuronal networks, and the computational capability of layered networks. May be coscheduled with PHYS 278.
