courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Recommended preparation: a working knowledge of calculus and linear algebra.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Research for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading or research on a problem by special arrangement with a faculty member. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor and departmental chair.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Honors Thesis Research for Undergraduates
courses.description: Honors thesis research for seniors participating in the Honors Program. Research is conducted under the supervision of a physics faculty member.
courses.prerequisites_text: admission to the Honors Program in Physics.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Advanced Classical Electrodynamics I
courses.description: A basic course in electromagnetism at the graduate level. Contents include special relativity, relativistic formulation of electrodynamics from the principle of least action, electrostatics, magnetostatics, multipoles, waves, light, diffraction, and multipole radiation.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Solid-State Physics II
courses.description: Deals with collective effects in solids arising from interactions between constituents. Topics include electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions, screening, band structure effects, Landau Fermi liquid theory. Magnetism in metals and insulators, superconductivity; occurrence, phenomenology, and microscopic theory.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 210A and PHYS 211A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics II
courses.description: Symmetry theory and conservation laws: time reversal, discrete, translation and rotational groups. Potential scattering. Time-dependent perturbation theory. Quantization of Electromagnetic fields and transition rates. Identical particles. Open systems: mixed states, dissipation, decoherence.
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 212A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Quantum Fields II
courses.description: Continued introduction to quantum fields including quantum loop contributions, renormalization, and the renormalization group. Additional topics including e.g., effective field theory, consequences of unitarity, operator product expansion, Anderson Higgs mechanism (abelian case).
courses.prerequisites_text: PHYS 215A.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: From time to time a member of the regular faculty or a resident visitor will find it possible to give a self-contained short course on an advanced topic in his or her special area of research. This course is not offered on a regular basis, but it is estimated that it will be given once each academic year. (S/U grades permitted.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Condensed Matter Physics Seminar
courses.description: Discussion of current research in physics of the solid state and of other condensed matter. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: High-Energy Physics Seminar
courses.description: Discussions of current research in nuclear physics, principally in the field of elementary particles. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Plasma Physics Seminar
courses.description: Discussions of recent research in plasma physics. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Astrophysics and Cosmology Seminar
courses.description: Discussions of recent research in astrophysics and cosmology. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Biophysics Seminar
courses.description: Presentation of current research in biological physics and quantitative biology by invited speakers from the United States and abroad. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit thirty times.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Physics Colloquium
courses.description: Discussions of recent research in physics directed to the entire physics community. (S/U grades only.)

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Biophysics of Neurons and Networks
courses.description: Information processing by nervous system through physical reasoning and mathematical analysis. A review of the biophysics of neurons and synapses and fundamental limits to signaling by nervous systems is followed by essential aspects of the dynamics of phase coupled neuronal oscillators, the dynamics and computational capabilities of recurrent neuronal networks, and the computational capability of layered networks. May be coscheduled with PHYS 178. Recommended preparation: a working knowledge of calculus and linear algebra.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Directed Study in Physics
courses.description: Research studies under the direction of a faculty member. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit up to twenty-four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: instructor and department approval required.

courses.subject: PHYS
courses.title: Thesis Research in Physics
courses.description: Directed research on dissertation topic. (S/U grades only.) May be taken for credit up to twenty-four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: instructor and department approval required.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-year Student Seminar
courses.description: The First-year Student Seminar Program is designed to provide new students with the opportunity to explore an intellectual topic with a faculty member in a small seminar setting. First-year student seminars are offered in all campus departments and undergraduate colleges, and topics vary from quarter to quarter. Enrollment is limited to fifteen to twenty students, with preference given to entering first-year students. May not be used to fulfill any major or minor requirements in political science.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Organized Interests
courses.description: This course provides a theoretical and practical examination of political parties, interest groups, and social movements in the United States.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics, Policy, and Educational Inequality
courses.description: Education is often thought of as “the great equalizer” but in the US and around the world, many governments fail to ensure that all citizens have access to high-quality educational opportunities. Why? This course will give students the conceptual tools to understand who shapes education policy decisions, through what channels, and how those policy decisions affect the quality and equity of education. Emphasis is on the US, but analyzed in comparative perspective.
courses.prerequisites_text: POLI 30 or POLI 30D.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Introduction to Legal Reasoning
courses.description: The ability to write and argue is one of the noted benefits of a legal education. Students will learn the basics of legal research and reasoning by learning to read and brief case law and write persuasive and objective memorandums.
courses.prerequisites_text: POLI 104A or 104B, upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Introduction to Business Law
courses.description: This course aims to introduce students to popular topics in business law. Structured as a survey course, this course will introduce students to the nature of business entities, contract formation, drafting, negotiations, negligence, and torts, as well as topics in intellectual property and employment law. The course will be structured as a lecture course, but will also provide students with ample opportunity for hands-on interactive practice.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Public Law: Special Topics
courses.description: This course is an opportunity for students to engage with and examine various topics on the theory, practice, and application of law. The content will vary according to recent developments in the field, as well as the particular research interests of the instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Sovereigns, Subjects, and the Modern State: Political Thought from Machiavelli to Rousseau
courses.description: The course deals with the period that marks the rise and triumph of the modern state. Central topics include the gradual emergence of human rights and the belief in individual autonomy. Readings from Machiavelli, Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, and others.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Economic Theories of Political Behavior
courses.description: An introduction to theories of political behavior developed with the assumptions and methods of economics. General emphasis will be upon theories linking individual behavior to institutional patterns. Specific topics to be covered will include collective action, leadership, voting, and bargaining.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Bending the Curve (Online): Solutions to Climate Change
courses.description: (Cross-listed with SIO 109R.) This online course focuses on developing urgent climate change solutions that integrate technology, policy and governance, finance, land use, and social/educational dimensions. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: POLI 117, POLI 117R, SIO 109, or SIO 109R.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics in Israel
courses.description: An interdisciplinary study of Israel as both a unique and yet a common example of a modern democratic nation-state. We will examine Israel’s history, its political, economic, and legal systems, social structure and multicultural tensions, the relation between state and religion, national security, and international relations.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics of Human Rights
courses.description: What do we mean by “international human rights”? Are they universal? This course examines human rights abuse and redress over time, and across different regions of the world. From this empirically grounded perspective, we critically evaluate contemporary human rights debates.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
courses.description: (Same as SOCI 188I.) In this course, we will examine the national and colonial dimensions of this long-lasting conflict and then turn our attention to the legal, governmental/political, and everyday aspects of the Israeli occupation of the West Bank and Gaza following the 1967 war.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics and Economics in Eastern Europe
courses.description: This course explores the interrelationship of politics and economics in Eastern Europe, analyzing the historic evolution of the area, the socialist period, and contemporary political and economic change there.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: How to Steal an Election
courses.description: Examine the role of elections in new and fragile democracies, explore how politicians construct elections to suppress increased levels of democracy, the techniques used to undermine free and fair elections, and the strategic responses to these actions by domestic/international actors.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics in the People’s Republic of China
courses.description: This course analyzes the political system of China since 1949, including political institutions, the policy-making process, and the relationship between politics and economics. The main focus is on the post-Mao era of reform beginning in 1978.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: A Sports Analytics Approach to the Social Sciences
courses.description: Sports analytics is a fast-growing field. It uses data and statistical methods to measure performance in competitive sports. The approach’s popularity has generated a wealth of data that can be used to shed light on social science questions in interesting ways. We will focus on topics such as violent behavior, discrimination, cultural/ethnic diversity, corruption, and cognitive biases using examples from baseball, basketball, figure skating, football, hockey, soccer, and sumo wrestling.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: National Security Strategy
courses.description: A survey of American strategies for national defense. Topics may include deterrence, coercive diplomacy, limited war, and unconventional warfare.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The European Union in World Politics
courses.description: This course introduces students to the role of the EU as a foreign policy actor. Topics include the development of the EU’s trade policy, foreign aid policy, security policy, as well as case studies of EU foreign policy.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Special Topics in Political Science Methodology
courses.description: Special topics course in quantitative methods for political science and broader social sciences. May be taken for credit up to three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Senior Honors Seminar: Frontiers of Political Science
courses.description: This course is open only to seniors interested in qualifying for departmental honors. Admission to the course will be determined by the department. Each student will write an honors essay under the supervision of a member of the faculty.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Research Seminar in Washington, DC
courses.description: (Same as COMM 194, USP 194, HITO 193, SOCI 194, COGS 194) Course attached to six-unit internship taken by students participating in the UCDC Program. Involves weekly seminar meetings with faculty and teaching assistant and a substantial research paper.
courses.prerequisites_text: participating in UCDC Program.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Local Internship in Political Science
courses.description: Individual placements for field learning integrated with political science. A written contract involving all parties with learning objectives, a project outline, and a means of supervision and progress evaluation must be filed with the faculty adviser and department undergraduate coordinator prior to the beginning of the internship. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: ninety units completed; 2.5 minimum cumulative GPA overall and 3.0 in political science; POLI 30 and at least two upper-division courses in political science. Department approval and consent of instructor. Corequisites: POLI 194SD.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Directed group study in an area not presently covered by the departmental curriculum. P/NP grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Research Apprenticeship
courses.description: Students conduct directed research as part of a principal investigator’s project and under the supervision of a department mentor. Students may conduct research with a department mentor for up to two quarters. This course is part of the Research Apprenticeship program in political science. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval. Students must apply for the Research Apprenticeship program and be approved to enroll. Participants must be majors in political science with junior or senior standing and a GPA of 3.5 or higher in all political science courses taken at UC San Diego. Individual projects may require other prerequisite training, such as POLI 30.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Independent Study for Undergraduates
courses.description: Independent reading in advanced political science by individual students. (P/NP grades only.)
courses.prerequisites_text: consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Analytic Theory I
courses.description: The first in the two-course sequence on the essentials of game theory and fundamental concepts in the social sciences. This course examines the philosophy of modeling, and introduces social choice theory, decision-making under uncertainty, and games of complete information. Applications include representation and democracy, social dilemmas and collective action, principal-agent problems, self-enforcing agreements, and institutions as equilibria.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate student standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Systems of Political Thought: Thucydides to Rousseau
courses.description: This course is a preparation for the field examination in political theory. It will provide an intensive and critical introduction to European political thought from Thucydides to Rousseau. Some of the secondary literature on this period will also be explored.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Comparative Politics: State and Society
courses.description: This course will provide a general literature review in comparative politics to serve as preparation for the field examination.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Understanding Authoritarianism
courses.description: This course offers an overview of topics in authoritarian politics. It explores a wide range of strategies authoritarian regimes employ to seize and consolidate power. Additionally, it delves into the distinctive challenges researchers encounter when conducting research in authoritarian contexts. We examine innovative research designs and recent methodological advancements that empower scholars to navigate these complexities.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Historical Political Economy
courses.description: Historical political economy (HPE) is a thriving field that employs quantitative historical datasets and qualitative case knowledge to study a wide range of political economy questions. Students will gain exposure to the frontiers of HPE research and will learn and apply historical research methods to a research project of their choice.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Special Topics in Comparative Politics
courses.description: This seminar is an examination of the different approaches to the study of comparative politics. Issues and research areas will vary each time the course is offered.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics of Development
courses.description: This course provides an overview of previous and current efforts to explain political and economic development in non-Western settings.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Relations Theory
courses.description: A survey of the principal theories and approaches to the study of international relations.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Formal Models in International Relations
courses.description: Explores formal analytic and primarily game-theoretic research in international relations with emphasis on conflict and bargaining. Topics include causes of war and peace, conventional and nuclear deterrence, crisis bargaining, arms race, and two-level games.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Special Topics in International Relations
courses.description: (Same as IRGN 290) This seminar is an examination of the different approaches to the study of international relations. Issues and research areas will vary each time the course is offered.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Race, Class, and Institutions in American Political Economy
courses.description: This course will explore how institutions address and/or perpetuate racial, ethnic, and economic inequality in the US.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Advanced Statistical Applications
courses.description: Use of advanced quantitative techniques in political science. Students will use political science data to complete small exercises and a major project. Students may not receive credit for both 271B and 271.
courses.prerequisites_text: 204B and 270; graduate standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Special Topics in Methodology
courses.description: This course offers selected topics in quantitative methodology. Content may vary each time the course is offered. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: International Law and Regulation
courses.description: Examination of recent research in international law and regulation: development and presentation of research projects by graduate students; presentation of research by faculty. Third-year students present dissertation prospectus, candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit three times as topics vary.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: American Politics
courses.description: Examination of recent research in American politics: development and presentation of research projects by graduate students, presentations of research by faculty. Third year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: Comparative Politics
courses.description: Examination of recent research in comparative politics, development and presentation of research projects by graduate students; presentations of research projects by faculty. Third-year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: International Relations
courses.description: Examination of recent research in international relations, development and presentation of research projects by graduate students, presentations of research projects by faculty. Third year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentation of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: Political Theory
courses.description: Examination of recent research in political theory: development and presentation of research projects by graduate students, presentation of research by faculty. Third year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Workshop: Methodology
courses.description: Examination of recent research in political methodology; development and presentation of research projects by graduate students, presentation of research by faculty. Third year students present dissertation prospectus; candidates make yearly presentations of dissertation research. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Directed Reading
courses.description: Guided and supervised reading in the literature of the several fields of political science.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: General Psychology: Biological Foundations
courses.description: This course provides an introductory survey of the relationship between human behavior and brain function. Specific areas of emphasis include vision and other sensory processes, memory, motivation, attention, and cognition.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: General Psychology: Cognitive Foundations
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the basic concepts of cognitive psychology. Topics include perception, attention, memory, language, and thought. The relation of cognitive psychology to cognitive science and to neuropsychology is also covered.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychosocial Foundations of the Climate Crisis
courses.description: Without action, global heating threatens to disrupt organized human existence. This class covers how global heating arose and its effects, why there is so little action by decision-makers, why some people are still skeptical about the facts and the need to respond, what justice demands, how to process our emotions, what kinds of policies are needed to cut emissions and to achieve community resilience in the face of climate and social damages, and why social mobilization is critical.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Introduction to Statistics
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to both descriptive and inferential statistics, core tools in the process of scientific discovery and the interpretation of research.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Methods in Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an overview of how to choose appropriate research methods for experimental and nonexperimental studies. Topics may include classic experimental design and counterbalancing, statistical power, and causal inference in experimental and nonexperimental settings.
courses.prerequisites_text: PSYC 60 or equivalent.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Laboratory in Psychological Research Methods
courses.description: This course provides hands-on research experience. Lecture topics will include experimental and nonexperimental designs, research ethics, data analysis, and causal inference. Students will design original research projects, collect and analyze data, and write a full APA-style report, including a brief literature review relevant to their design. This course builds on PSYC 70 by applying design principles to students’ own research questions and ideas. Open to the following Department of Psychology majors only: PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, COGS 14B or PSYC 60 or MATH 11 and PSYC 70 or COGS 14A.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study or research under direction of a member of the faculty. May be taken up to three times for a maximum of twelve units.
courses.prerequisites_text: lower-division standing, completion of at least thirty units of undergraduate study at UC San Diego with a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0; completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the field of developmental psychology, including topics in cognitive, language, and social development.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Sensory Neuroscience
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the neural mechanisms that support vision, audition, touch, olfaction, and taste.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of cognitive psychology, the scientific study of mental processes: how people acquire, store, transform, use, and communicate information. Topics may include perception, attention, language, memory, reasoning, problem solving, decision-making, and creativity.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Behavioral Neuroscience
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of human and animal behavior from a neuroscience perspective. Topics include the functions and mechanisms of perception, motivation (sex, sleep, hunger, emotions), learning and memory, and motor control and movement.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of neuroanatomy and major methods and results from neuroimaging and neuropsychological studies of behavior. Topics include attention, motor control, executive function, memory, learning, emotion, and language.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Juniors Honors Research Seminars
courses.description: This course provides research seminars by a range of departmental faculty, exposing students to contemporary research problems in many areas of psychology. Class discussions will follow faculty presentations. Must be taken for a letter grade for the Psychology Honors Program.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Admission by application. Department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Methods I
courses.description: This course provides training in applying advanced statistical methods to experimental design. Emphasis will be placed on the developing skills in statistical problem-solving, using computer applications, and writing scientific reports. Must be taken for a letter grade for the Psychology Honors Program.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing. Open to honors students or by consent of instructor. Instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Health Sciences Research
courses.description: In this course, students explore major models in mental health research and apply them in laboratory settings, examining how team science generates knowledge and influences society. Through literature review and focused discussions on study design, methodology, and research ethics, they develop skills in critical analysis and proposal writing. If interested, students with satisfactory performance may continue research with the PI for academic credit by pursuing PSYC 199 in health sciences.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Clinical Neuropsychology
courses.description: This course provides a fundamental understanding of brain-behavior relationships as applied to the practice of clinical neuropsychology. Major topics include functional neuroanatomy, principles of neuropsychological assessment and diagnosis, and the neuropsychological presentation of common neurologic and psychiatric conditions.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Cognition
courses.description: This course provides an overview of social cognition, which blends cognitive and social psychology to understand how people make sense of the social world. Topics may include social perception, inference, memory, motivation, affect, understanding the self, stereotypes, and cultural cognition.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Memory and Amnesia
courses.description: This course will provide a survey of current research and theory concerning human memory and amnesia from both cognitive and neuropsychological perspectives. Topics may include short-term (working) memory, encoding and retrieval, episodic and semantic memory, interference and forgetting, false memory, eyewitness memory, emotion and memory, famous case studies of amnesia, and the effects of aging and dementia on memory.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Educational Psychology
courses.description: What do we know about how students learn, and what does that tell us about how to design effective instruction? Topics will include principles of learning, learning in subject matter areas, motivation, development of learning and thinking strategies, individual differences, and classroom processes.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Tests and Measurement
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to psychology testing. Topics include psychometrics and statistical methods of test construction; application of psychological tests in industry, clinical practice, and applied settings; and controversies in the application of psychological tests.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing; COGS 14B or MATH 11 or PSYC 60.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Emotion
courses.description: This course provides an overview of past and current theories of emotion. Topics include facial expressions associated with emotion, psychophysiology, evolutionary perspectives, and specific emotions such as anger, fear, and jealousy.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Behavior Modification
courses.description: The course provides an extension of learning principles to human behavior. Topics include broad implications of a behavioral perspective, applied behavior analysis, and applications of behavioral principles to clinical disorders and to normal behavior in varied settings.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Health Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an exploration of health, illness, and treatment as they relate to psychological concepts and considers how stress influences the body’s physiological systems and risk for physical illnesses.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology and the Law
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the intersection between psychology and the legal system, covering a broad range of forensically relevant issues. Topics may include false memories, false confessions, eyewitness reliability, lie detection, DNA exonerations of the wrongfully convicted, jury decision making, and neuroscience and the law. Recommended preparation: PSYC 60.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychological Disorders of Childhood
courses.description: This course provides an overview of psychological disorders in children. Topics may include anxiety disorders, depressive and bipolar disorders, communication and learning disorders, conduct problems, autism, and other conditions. Emphasis is placed on symptomatology, assessment, etiological factors, epidemiology, and treatment.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Human Sexuality
courses.description: This course provides an overview of human sexuality research including diversity of sexual behavior and identities, sex and gender development, intimate relationships, and sexual dysfunction. Recommended preparation: completion of PSYC 1, 2, or 106.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Mindfulness and Well-being
courses.description: This course provides a review of the scientific research surrounding the topic of mindfulness, which has been approached from multiple disciplines including Buddhism, positive psychology, cognitive behavioral therapy, and neuroscience. Because mindfulness is so multifaceted with many variables involved, the scientific study of mindfulness requires rigorous research methods and statistics, and for this reason a significant portion of the class focuses on these aspects.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, COGS 14B or MATH 11 or PSYC 60, and COGS 14A or PSYC 70. Department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Drugs, Addiction, and Mental Disorders
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the use, abuse, liability, and psychotherapeutic effects of drugs on humans.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychopharmacology—Drugs and Behavior
courses.description: This course provides an overview of basic principles of psychopharmacology, including psychological effects, brain mode of action, and patterns of use of psychoactive agents. Drugs discussed may include drugs of abuse and psychotherapeutics such as stimulants, opioids, sedative hypnotics, hallucinogens, marijuana, alcohol, cognitive enhancers, anxiolytics, antidepressants, and antipsychotics.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Choice and Self-Control
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the experimental analysis of choice behavior, with an emphasis on the types of choice involved in self-control. A central interest will be the conditions under which decision-making is optimal.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Development of Social Cognition
courses.description: This course provides an overview of how children learn to reason about the social world. Topics may include theory of mind, social categorization and stereotyping, moral reasoning, and cultural learning. Recommended preparation: PSYC 101.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Sleep
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the psychology of sleep, including sleep stages and their functions, neurological aspects of sleep, sleep across species and development, dreams and their interpretation, sleep disorders, and the role of sleep in learning and memory.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Topics in Psychology
courses.description: Selected topics in the field of psychology. May be taken for credit three times as topics vary.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology Laboratory Topics
courses.description: Selected laboratory topics in the field of psychology. May be taken for credit two times as topics vary. Open to the following majors only: PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33, PC34, CG32.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, department approval, and PSYC 60 or COGS 14B or MATH 11 and PSYC 70 or COGS 14A.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Honors Thesis II
courses.description: This course provides the opportunity for students to continue to carry out their research projects. Must be taken for a letter grade for the Psychology Honors Program.
courses.prerequisites_text: PSYC 110, PSYC 111A-B, PSYC 194A, department approval, psychology majors only, acceptance to the Honors program.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Seminar
courses.description: Weekly research seminar, three quarter research project under faculty guidance which culminates in a thesis. Must be taken for a letter grade to satisfy major requirements for Department of Psychology majors. Open to the following majors only: PC25, PC26, PC28, PC29, PC30, PC31, PC32, PC33, PC34, PC35.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study or laboratory research under direction of faculty in the Department of Psychology. P/NP grades only. May be taken for credit nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing and department approval.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Quantitative Methods in Psychology II
courses.description: The second part of a series of intensive courses in statistical methods and the mathematical treatment of data, with special reference to research in psychology.
courses.prerequisites_text: PSYC 201A.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Department Proseminar
courses.description: This course is required of all first-year students in the PhD program and serves as an introduction to the department faculty and their research programs. In this course, one psychology faculty member will lead one session on their research and area of expertise, including assigned readings of relevant journal articles.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Area Proseminar: The Methods of Human Cognitive Neuroscience
courses.description: Covers many of the neuroscience methods available to study human cognition, with emphasis on concepts of data analysis, and comparative assessment of the different methods (along with alternative nonhuman animal approaches), with an eye to pitfalls and interpretational limitations.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Cognitive Neural Systems (CNS)
courses.description: A weekly seminar series focused on understanding recent advances in the relationship between neural systems and behavior using a variety of experimental approaches (single unit recording, comp neuro, evolutionary bio, psychophysics, comparative anatomy, lesion work, psychopharm, fMRI, EEG, TMS, etc.). May be taken for credit twenty-four times.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing. S/U grades only.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Developmental Psychology
courses.description: Advanced seminar concentrating on methods of research and current experimental literature in developmental psychology. May be taken for credit twenty-four times. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Learning by Thinking in Children (and Adults)
courses.description: We often learn through observations or from testimony from others. Occasionally, we learn simply by thinking. How do we generate insights in the absence of new information from the external world? This course examines the cognitive capacities involved in learning by thinking, including thought experiments, deduction, analogy, imagination, and learning by explaining. This discussion-based seminar will take a cognitive science approach, emphasizing cognitive development.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Introduction to Laboratory Experimentation II
courses.description: Continuation of basic laboratory course designed to introduce first-year graduate students to experimental methods in psychology. The student will select a research topic; do a thorough literature review of the area; design and carry out new, original studies of problems in the selected area; and prepare a final formal report of the study at the end of the spring quarter. This course is required of all first-year graduate students in the department. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Selected Topics in Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: An in-depth analysis of selected empirical and theoretical topics in cognitive psychology. The course will focus on areas where notable progress appears to be taking place in contemporary research.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Social Psychology
courses.description: A biweekly seminar series focusing on recent advances in both basic and applied research in social psychology including topics such as interpersonal relationships, emotion, health, social cognition, judgment, and decision making. May be taken for credit twenty-four times. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Current Directions in Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: A weekly seminar series focused on understanding recent advances in any area of cognitive psychology. May be taken for credit twenty-four times. S/U grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: graduate standing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Seminar in Communication and Information Processing
courses.description: S/U grades only.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Practicum
courses.description: Research in psychology under supervision of individual faculty members. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit fifteen times.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Practicum
courses.description: Independent research and thesis research. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit fifteen times.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: Teaching practicum for students enrolled in graduate program in psychology. Students who hold appointments as teaching assistants must enroll in this course. Minimum program requirement is for one four-unit course per year for four years. S/U grades only.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Public Health
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to the infrastructure of public health; the analytical tools employed by public health practitioners; bio-psychosocial perspectives of public health problems; health promotion/disease prevention; quality assessment in public health; and legal and ethical concerns. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 40. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 40 and PH 40.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Methods and Ethics in Public Health Research
courses.description: This course will lay a foundation for understanding how to conduct research to answer questions about public health. It aims to teach students why research is done the way it is, what questions we can and can’t answer, and the methodological and ethical limits that must be considered along the way. Students will learn to think critically about the implications and limitations of existing research, and to form their own research questions about public health and the ways to investigate answers.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Learning Sustainable Well-Being: Compassion for Self and Others, a Public Health Perspective
courses.description: This experiential course teaches the art of practicing psychological well-being, based on Eastern and Western approaches (e.g., mindfulness, positive psychology, cognitive therapy, neuroscience, theatre and art), from the perspective of public health. Each week there is a short lecture on a given topic, combined with workshop-style exercises. This course is part of the Learning Sustainable Well-being Program. Visit lsw.ucsd.edu for more information.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Exploring Public Health
courses.description: This seminar-style course offers students the opportunity to explore key areas of public health, covering foundational principles across a variety of topics. Subjects range and may include, but are not limited to, career pathways in public health, strategies for maintaining well-being and academic success, mental health awareness and support, sexual health and reproductive rights, mindfulness practices, financial wellness, stress management, and more.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Selected topics in the field of public health.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Individual undergraduate study or research not covered by the present course offerings. May be taken for credit three times.
courses.prerequisites_text: completion of thirty units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 3.0, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Epidemiology
courses.description: This course covers the basic principles of epidemiology, with applications to investigations of noninfectious (“chronic”) and infectious diseases. Explores various study designs appropriate for disease surveillance and studies of etiology and prevention. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 101. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 101 and PH 101.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and PSYC 60, HDS 60, MATH 11, or COGS 14B, and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Health Behavior and Chronic Diseases
courses.description: This course introduces health behavior concepts through applications to chronic disease prevention. The focus is on smoking, dietary behaviors, and physical activity and is organized around relationships to health, measurement, influencing factors, interventions, and translation to public health practice. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 110. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 110 and PH 110.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Health Policies for Healthy Lifestyles
courses.description: This course covers the rationale for and effectiveness of policies to influence nutrition, physical activity, and substance use behavior. Policies include legalization, taxation, labeling, produce manufacturing, warning labels, licensing, marketing, and counter-marketing practices and restrictions on use. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 120. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 120 and PH 120.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Environmental and Occupational Health
courses.description: This core public health course addresses the fundamentals of environmental and occupational health, including identification of hazards, basic toxicology, risk assessment, prevention/protection, and regulatory/control policies. Specific environmental and occupational hazards and relevant case studies will be presented. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major. Renumbered from FMPH 130. Students may not receive credit for FMPH 130 and PH 130.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 101 or FMPH 101, and upper-division standing.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Clinical Nutrition in Public Health
courses.description: Clinical nutrition is the study of nutrition and diet as related to the prevention and treatment of human disease. The practical and psychosocial aspects of diet modification and food/food product availability are key aspects of clinical nutrition practice, whether individual or community based, irrespective of whether the goal is primary prevention or disease treatment. Students will identify applications and translation of nutritional guidelines and recommendations into behavior in the course. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40. Restricted enrollment to sophomore, junior, and senior standing. Renumbered from FMPH 161. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 161 and PH 161.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Immunizations and Public Health
courses.description: This course addresses fundamentals of vaccine-preventable diseases and immunizations, with an emphasis on resources to maintain public health expertise in a continually evolving field.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40 and sophomore standing. Renumbered from FMPH 191. Students can’t receive credit for FMPH 172 if they have already completed FMPH 191 subtitled “Immunizations and Public Health.”

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Health Capstone I
courses.description: This is the first of a two-part capstone series that serves as the culminating experience for the BS in public health (BSPH) majors. Students will integrate the skills and knowledge gained throughout the BSPH program and learn critical elements of public health research and practice. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 45, PH 101 or FMPH 101, PH 102 or FMPH 102, PH 110 or FMPH 110, and PH 120 or FMPH 120. Department approval required. Restricted to senior public health majors only. Renumbered from FMPH 193. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: PH 193, PH 193R, or FMPH 193.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Health Capstone II
courses.description: This is the second of a two-part capstone series that serves as the culminating experience for the BS in public health (BSPH) majors. Students will interpret and contextualize findings from their projects completed in the first part of the series. Oral and written presentations will focus on disseminating public health information in diverse formats. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 45, PH 101 or FMPH 101, PH 102 or FMPH 102, PH 110 or FMPH 110, PH 120 or FMPH 120, and PH 193 or FMPH 193. Department approval required. Restricted to senior public health majors only. Renumbered from FMPH 194. Students may only receive credit for one of the following: PH 194, PH 194R, or FMPH 194.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Pedagogy and Learning Apprenticeship
courses.description: Under the supervision of an instructor, undergraduate students gain teaching experience through practical experiences in course management and effective teaching methods. May be taken for credit up to two times.
courses.prerequisites_text: a minimum of A– in the course in which the student plans to assist, a 3.0 cumulative UC GPA, and instructor and department approval.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Health Honors Practicum I
courses.description: This is the first of an accelerated two-part honors series that serves as the culminating experience for the BS in public health (BSPH) majors. Students review, reinforce, and complement skills and knowledge gained throughout the BSPH program, and prepare a proposal integrating critical elements of public health research and practice. This course represents an experiential learning opportunity at a pre-approved community site. Students will develop, refine, and implement a public health proposal. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the public health major.
courses.prerequisites_text: PH 40 or FMPH 40, PH 45, PH 101 or FMPH 101, PH 102 or FMPH 102, PH 110 or FMPH 110, PH 120 or FMPH 120. Department approval required. Restricted to upper-division public health majors only.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Directed Group Study
courses.description: Investigation of public health topics through directed reading and discussion by a small group of students. Opportunities can also include experiential and research components. Study must be under supervision of a faculty member and approval must be secured from the faculty member prior to registering. P/NP grades only. Renumbered from FMPH 198. PH 198 and/or FMPH 198 may be taken for credit a combined total of nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Individual undergraduate study or research not covered by the present course offerings. Study or research must be under the direction of a faculty member in the Department of Family Medicine and Public Health and approval must be secured from the faculty member prior to registering. P/NP grades only. Renumbered from FMPH 199. PH 199 and/or FMPH 199 may be taken for credit a combined total of nine times.
courses.prerequisites_text: upper-division standing, completion of ninety units of UC San Diego undergraduate study, a minimum UC San Diego GPA of 2.5, consent of instructor, and a completed and approved Special Studies form.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Scientific Writing
courses.description: Students will learn the principles of scientific writing, review examples of scientific literature, and then complete a manuscript suitable for publication based on their research project.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: HSRIS Colloquium Series
courses.description: The HSRIS colloquium series is a program of empirical research seminars focused on the most important issues facing patients, providers, health care systems, and policymakers today. It provides an opportunity for HSRIS doctoral students across all stages of completion to meet regularly, analyze and critique ongoing research, and participate in stimulating discussion with HSRIS faculty and guest lecturers.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Addressing Health Equity through Policy
courses.description: Public health policy is what public officials within government, and by extension the citizens they represent, choose to do or not to do about public health problems. This course provides an overview of the U.S. health policy landscape and addresses the development of explicit health policies to promote certain health behaviors, policies aimed at public health safety, and policy issues related to emerging health and biomedical technologies.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Topics of special interest in public health. Topics may vary from quarter to quarter.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Independent Study in Public Health
courses.description: Individual graduate study or research not covered by present course offerings. Study or research must be under the direction of a faculty member in the School of Public Health and approval must be secured from the faculty member and track director prior to registering.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Dissertation Research in Public Health
courses.description: Public health doctoral program dissertation research units.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Health Policy
courses.description: This course will introduce students to health policy making and the organization and financing of health services in the United States, enhance their understanding of the historical and political context of health policy, and enable them to develop strategies for analysis of health policy issues. The course aims to convey not just specific facts, but to help students develop the ability and confidence to assess current health policy issues in a thoughtful, comprehensive, and rigorous manner.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 405. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 405 and PH 405.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Scientific Writing
courses.description: This course will prepare students for scientific writing in a variety of contexts. These may include scientific abstracts and research summaries, plain language summaries, op-eds, community engagement, and using LLMs. The course will incorporate group projects as well as individual assignments.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 406. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 406 and PH 406.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Program Optimization and Evaluation
courses.description: This course covers study designs to iteratively optimize and evaluate public health programs such as a proof-of-concept trial, randomized controlled trial, sequential multiple assignment randomized trial, factorial screening trial, microrandomized trial, stepped wedge trial, single case experiments, and nonrandomized study designs. The course includes a philosophical grounding on why evidence is important and what underlying assumptions undergird “evidence-based practice.”
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB87, PB90, and PB75) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 402 or PH 402, and FMPH 403 or PH 403. Renumbered from FMPH 411. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 411 and PH 411.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Health Promotion and Communication
courses.description: This course is focused on the principles of health promotion and health communication, examining the societal impact and needs, behavioral change theory, and study designs to develop and evaluate interventions. Effective communication techniques used to promote behavior change, disseminate evidence, and communicate risk in today’s multimedia world are highlighted, including cultural tailoring. Students serially develop and apply these strategies in the design of a public health campaign of their choice.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, and PB90) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 402 or PH 402. Renumbered from FMPH 412. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 412 and PH 412.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Ethics in Public Health Research and Practice
courses.description: The first section of this course provides an introduction to key frameworks and concepts relevant to public health ethics. The remaining part of the course considers ethical dilemmas across resource allocation and distributive justice, individual rights versus the common good, health promotion and disease prevention, free markets versus social justice, research ethics, emerging public health technologies and interventions, and public health and the environment.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in the MPH program (PB91, PB87, PB88, PB90, and PB75) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 413. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 413 and PH 413.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Advanced Epidemiologic Methods
courses.description: This course will provide an in-depth overview of modern epidemiologic concepts, including fundamentals of causal inference; quantitative measures of occurrence, association, and effect; epidemiologic study design; epidemiologic data analysis; sources of bias in epidemiologic studies; and design and analytic strategies for the evaluation and mitigation of bias in epidemiologic studies.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 401 or PH 401. Renumbered from FMPH 415. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 415 and PH 415.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Biostatistics II
courses.description: Students will understand and conduct advanced bio-statistical analyses including: multiple linear and logistic regression, survival analysis, Cox and extended Cox regression, and longitudinal data analysis. Students will analyze data using these techniques and learn to program using a statistical software package (e.g., R). Issues such as confounding, missing data, and causal inference will be discussed.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 400 or PH 400. Renumbered from FMPH 419. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 419 and PH 419.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Mental Health Epidemiology
courses.description: This course focuses on public health approaches to studying mental illnesses nationally and globally. Course content will include an overview of global mental health epidemiology; research methods; vulnerable populations, such as refugees and immigrants; and the challenges and future opportunities to address the mental illness epidemic, taking into consideration the social and cultural diversity within study populations.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB89, and PB91) or program approval and successfully completed FMPH 401 or PH 401. Renumbered from FMPH 425. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 425 and PH 425.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Dissemination and Implementation, Policy, and Health Services in Mental Health
courses.description: This course will use a dissemination and implementation science methodology and lens to address the gap between promising research results for mental health and their successful translation into improved individual, community, and population health. Real-world case examples and a multidisciplinary approach will be used to discuss and address factors that impact the adoption, implementation, and sustained use of specific health-related interventions.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB88, and PB89) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 428. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 428 and PH 428.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Design and Public Health
courses.description: The focus of this project-based class is on teaching students fundamentals in design, with a particular focus on human-centered design and community-centered design. By the end of the course, students will have developed personal skills in using their chosen design approach (human- or community-centered design) and worked to advance and provide support to real-world partners of the professor. Students will also engage in a self-study project.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75 and PB90) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 460. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 460 and PH 460.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Introduction to Foundation and Government Grant Writing (Non-NIH)
courses.description: Students learn the skill of grant writing as used by academics, practitioners, and leaders of the public health community to support program development and implementation, technical assistance and capacity building, resource development, research projects, training programs, and other areas. Students will learn strategies for successful teamwork and be introduced to strategies to identify and respond to grant opportunities using a data-driven and theoretically sound approach.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91).

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Course will cover various topics in the field of public health. May be taken for credit up to twelve times for a maximum of forty-eight units.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval. Renumbered from FMPH 491.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: MPH Practicum Field Placement
courses.description: This course provides MPH students the opportunity to participate in a short-term, field-based public health or population-based experience. Students will engage in a field experience in collaboration with a sponsoring organization and qualified site mentor. Students are expected to apply theory, skills, and training acquired through the public health course work within a real-life setting. Students will develop written and oral communication skills that employ public health concepts and methods.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91). Renumbered from FMPH 496B. Students may not receive credit for both FMPH 496B and PH 496B.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Independent study under the guidance of a Wertheim School of Public Health faculty member. May be taken for credit up to twelve times for a maximum of forty-eight units.
courses.prerequisites_text: program approval required.

courses.subject: PH
courses.title: Public Health Master’s Capstone/Thesis
courses.description: Students complete their capstone/thesis, and potentially submit their capstone/thesis for publication and/or present their capstone/thesis to stakeholders. May be taken for credit up to six times.
courses.prerequisites_text: must be enrolled in MPH program (PB75, PB87, PB88, PB89, PB90, and PB91) or program approval.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistical Methods II
courses.description: Intermediate-level graduate course in the analysis of categorical data. Topics include generalized linear models (logistic, Poisson, loglinear models); maximum likelihood and quasi likelihood approaches; model diagnostics, computational approaches and inferential strategies. Both theory and practice will be addressed. Renumbered from FMPH 222. Students may not receive credit for PHB 222 and FMPH 222. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the biostatistics degree requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of FMPH 221 or PHB 221 and FMPH 244A or PHB 244A or MATH 281A or program approval.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Statistical Methods for Observational Studies
courses.description: An introduction to inference and causal modeling for observational data, including propensity score adjustment, inverse probability weighting, instrumental variables, and sensitivity analysis. Data analysis and computation will be required. Must be taken for a letter grade to be applied to the biostatistics degree requirements. Renumbered from FMPH 226. Students may not receive credit for PHB 226 and FMPH 226.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of FMPH 221 or PHB 221, FMPH 222 or PHB 222, and FMPH 223 or PHB 223 or program approval.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistics Rotation
courses.description: This practicum provides hand-on experience with biomedical research and data analysis. Working within a specific biomedical domain (e.g., cancer, genomics, or physical activity research), students will conduct original data analysis and prepare or substantially contribute to a final project report. Renumbered from FMPH 241. PHB 241 and/or FMPH 241 may be taken for credit for a combined total of five times.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of FMPH 221 or PHB 221 and FMPH 222 or PHB 222; biostatistics major only.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Practicum in Biostatistics B
courses.description: This is the second in a sequence of two core courses for the MS degree in biostatistics. The course takes advantage of the extensive involvement of the program faculty in collaborative and interdisciplinary work within the life sciences. Didactic instruction on best practices in statistical collaboration. Under supervision, the students will participate in applied, real-life projects stemming from the research and collaborations of the faculty in the Division of Biostatistics. Renumbered from FMPH 243B. Students may not receive credit for PHB 243B and FMPH 243B.
courses.prerequisites_text: successful completion of FMPH 243A or PHB 243B. Restricted to major code PB76.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Foundations in Biostatistics B
courses.description: Continued overview of mathematical foundations in biostatistics. The second course in a two-course series. Maximum likelihood theory. Sufficiency, efficiency. Hypothesis testing and confidence intervals. Robustness and power. Large-sample properties of commonly-used estimators and tests. Renumbered from FMPH 244B. Students may not receive credit for PHB 244B and FMPH 244B. Must be taken for a letter grade if applied to biostatistics degree requirements.
courses.prerequisites_text: FMPH 244A or PHB 244A, restricted to major code PB76.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistics Journal Club
courses.description: This is a biweekly, structured journal club. Students will critically read assigned articles. During meetings, students work in groups to discuss specific questions regarding the assigned article, and are asked to present their answers to the class. Renumbered from FMPH 290. PHB 280 and/or FMPH 290 may be taken for credit for a combined total of six times. Restricted to major codes PB76 or PB77.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Biostatistics Seminar Series
courses.description: Through a combination of in-person and virtual seminars on Zoom, students will gain insight into current research projects presented by invited speakers. Additionally, students are provided with the opportunity to participate in lunch discussions and one-on-one meetings. All MS students in biostatistics, and biostatistics PhD students in their third year and above are highly encouraged to enroll quarterly (except for summer). May be taken for credit up to twelve times.
courses.prerequisites_text: FMPH 290 or PHB 280. Restricted to PB76 and PB77 majors.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Independent study for biostatistics graduate students in the Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science. Study of special topics for graduate students under the direction of a faculty member. Exact subject matter to be arranged in individual cases. Restricted to PB76 and PB77 majors. May be taken for credit up to twenty-one times.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval required.

courses.subject: PHB
courses.title: Dissertation Research
courses.description: Dissertation research for students who are advancing or have advanced to candidacy. May be taken for credit up to twelve times. Renumbered from FMPH 299. PHB 299 and/or FMPH 299 may be taken for credit for a combined total of twelve times.
courses.prerequisites_text: department approval required.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Advanced Financial Risk Management
courses.description: Introduces ways to identify, measure, estimate, and control risks in the context of risk management as applied in fixed income, foreign exchange, and equity markets. Reviews the pricing and hedging applications of derivatives, such as futures, options, and CDSs. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Valuation in Corporate Finance
courses.description: Covering the fundamentals of corporate finance and their application to valuation (including the WACC approach, APV approach, multiples, and real option valuation). We focus on important areas of corporate finance, including capital structure, real options, and financial distress and bankruptcy. Letter grades only. Students may not receive credit for both MGTF 407 and MGT 487.
courses.prerequisites_text: MGTF 402; restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: New Venture Finance
courses.description: Focuses on the financing of new ventures and technological innovation. Includes perspectives of both the entrepreneur and the investor, investigating the venture capital process, and methods of financial valuation useful in the venture capital industry and for other technology investments. Letter grades only. Students may not receive credit for both MGTF 410 and MGT 493.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Financial Statement Analysis
courses.description: Develop a deeper familiarity with financial accounting and assumptions underlying measurements reported in financial statements. Understanding of economic and regulatory forces underlying corporate disclosure of financial statements. Knowledge of data sources and analytical tools to extract and evaluate this data. Letter grades only. Students may not receive credit for both MGTF 412 and MGT 494.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Computational Finance Methods
courses.description: This course introduces students to a variety of mathematical methods as applied in finance, including Monte Carlo simulation, optimization methods, and numerical solution to PDEs. Letter grades only.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Professional Seminars in Finance
courses.description: Discussion series involving industry experts, alumni, and executives on current issues in financial services. Educates students on industry trends. Prepares students to be effective users of the financial press and to be effective in discussion and interaction with financial professionals. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit two times. Students may not earn credit for both MGTF 416 and MGT 401.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Professional Communications in Finance
courses.description: Focuses on communications skills and abilities required for effective professionals in the financial services sector. Addresses oral and written communications, including presentations, informational and job interviewing, resume writing, cross-cultural communication, and report writing. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit two times. Students may not earn credit for both MGTF 417 and MGT 402.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Corporate Finance
courses.description: The course covers the foundations of finance with emphasis on corporate finance applications. Discussion of the major financial decisions made by managers both within the firm and in interactions with investors. Essential in most of these decisions is the process of valuation which is an important emphasis of the course.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Derivatives and Structured Finance
courses.description: Provides an overview of options, futures, swaps, and other derivatives, many of which are now commonplace in financial markets. Discussion around examples of how derivatives are used to solve particular problems in practice, as well as the underlying pricing methodologies.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Data Science for Finance
courses.description: Introduction to a collection of powerful, open-source tools needed to manage and analyze data and to conduct data science in finance applications. Course will give an overview of the basic process of data science and dive into the data management and machine learning techniques useful for financial data analysis.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGTF
courses.title: Special Topics in Finance
courses.description: Introduces advanced topics of special interest in finance. Instructional methods can include face-to-face lecture, case presentations, assigned teaching, and/or online group discussions. May be taken for credit up to four times. Students may not earn credit when course subtitles are the same.
courses.prerequisites_text: restricted to master of quantitative finance program or with instructor approval or department approval.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Quantitative Methods in Business
courses.description: Introduction to techniques to develop/analyze data for informed tactical and strategic management decisions: statistical inference, probability, regression analysis, and optimization. Using these analytic approaches, theory-based formulas, and spreadsheets, students explore managerial applications across all areas of business activity.

courses.subject: MGT
courses.title: Financial Accounting
